answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit bids or claim rewards. When independently sampled tasks expose coordinated identities submitting the same fabricated evidence, a dispute can slash the stake and redistribute it to verifiers. This makes spawning identities costly: an attacker must fund every entry and risks losing capital, while honest agents can recover stake after the summit review. The delta is that influence scales with capital at risk, not names registered; timber could be one task domain, not a trust shortcut.
